title: The Fall of Constantinople
description: April-May 1453. The player commands the last defenders of Byzantium under Constantine XI. Hold the Theodosian Walls against Mehmed II's siege: repair breaches from bombard fire, guard the sea walls along the Golden Horn, and survive repeated assaults. Defeat comes if the Hagia Sophia district falls; victory means holding until the final assault is broken.

anachronisms_found: SALADIN hero placed as the Ottoman commander: Saladin was a Kurdish Ayyubid sultan who died in 1193, 260 years before 1453, and had nothing to do with the Ottomans; the engine offers a generic Sultan/hero or simply a named King unit to stand in for Mehmed II, so this was avoidable
Mehmed II is never represented by any placed object despite dominating the dialogue - only Saladin stands in for him
CAMEL_RIDER x3 in the Ottoman roster: the Turkish civilisation has no camel units, and camel cavalry is not part of an Ottoman siege army operating in Thrace
TREE_PALM_FOREST x10 as the map's only tree type: Constantinople's Thracian hinterland is Mediterranean woodland, not palm desert; oak/pine/Mediterranean tree sets exist in the editor
The Ottoman assault force is built of generic ARCHER and SPEARMAN while the text announces 'Janissary regulars' - the Janissary unit and Hand Cannoneers were both available and unused
No water, ships, or sea walls anywhere on the map despite the brief and objectives explicitly requiring the player to 'guard the sea walls along the Golden Horn'

issues_found: Player TWO's commander is the SALADIN hero unit — a 12th-century Ayyubid sultan standing in for Mehmed II, who died 260 years before 1453. The engine ships no Mehmed hero, so a renamed generic (e.g. a Cavalry Archer or Elite Janissary-equivalent) was the correct choice; placing a different named historical figure is avoidable error.

Both players are set to civilization RANDOM, so Byzantine and Turkish architecture, tech trees and unit bonuses are not guaranteed — the engine offers exactly Byzantines and Turks for this battle, making this a purely avoidable omission.

Ottoman roster includes CAMEL_RIDER x3, an Arab/Saracen unit inappropriate for the Rumelian and Anatolian troops at Constantinople, while the engine's Janissary (referenced in the text: 'Janissary regulars pour through the breach') is nowhere placed.
TREE_PALM_FOREST x10 is the vegetation placed for Thrace/the Bosphorus — palms are wrong for the Marmara littoral in April.

No water tiles, ships, or sea walls are present despite the brief and the objectives promising defence of the Golden Horn sea walls; the naval dimension (the chain, the Ottoman fleet portage, the Genoese relief squadron) is entirely absent.

Ottoman force is absurdly small (roughly 22 starting units plus a handful of waves) against a besieging army the sources put at 50,000–80,000; the asymmetry that defined the siege is inverted, with the defenders' 23 units nearly matching the attackers.
Only 3 bombard cannon and 2 mangonels represent Mehmed's siege train of some 60–70 guns including the Orban supergun; the 'great bombard roars' text is not matched by any distinguished large gun.
The Theodosian Walls are a single 57-tile stone wall line with no representation of the double wall, outer wall and moat that made the fortification famous.

SALADIN is placed as the Ottoman commander standing in for Mehmed II — a 12th-century Kurdish/Ayyubid figure representing a 15th-century Ottoman sultan. The engine ships no Mehmed hero, but a renamed generic unit (as was done for Constantine with KING) was available, so this substitution is avoidable and doubly wrong in both culture and era.

Both players are set to RANDOM civilization, so neither Byzantine nor Turkish architecture, unit bonuses, or the Turks' gunpowder identity is guaranteed — a wholly avoidable omission given the engine explicitly ships both civs.

CAMEL_RIDER x3 in the Ottoman order of battle is Saracen/desert flavour, not the Janissary-and-azap composition the narration itself describes; no HAND_CANNONEER or other gunpowder infantry stands in for the Janissaries the text names as pouring through the breach.
TREE_PALM_FOREST x10 and CLIFF objects are wrong flora and terrain for Thracian Constantinople.

The brief promises defence of the sea walls along the Golden Horn, but there is no water, no DOCK, no ships, and no naval element anywhere in the 196 placed objects — the Ottoman fleet, the chain boom, and the hauling of ships overland are entirely absent.

Only three GATE_NORTH_TO_SOUTH and a single 57-tile stone wall line represent the triple Theodosian Walls with their moat and outer wall; the layered defence that defined the siege is flattened to one curtain.

The victory condition requires the DESTRUCTION of Player 1's own MONASTERY (the Hagia Sophia proxy) in conjunction with the 600s timer, while the same object's destruction is simultaneously a defeat trigger — the goal encoding contradicts itself on the very building the scenario says the fight is over.
SHEEP x12, GOLD_MINE x10, STONE_MINE x8 and FORAGE_BUSH x8 give the besieged city an open economy it did not have; a starving blockaded capital should be resource-poor.
